The search results show that Tauri 2.0 added iOS and Android support and reached stable status, though mobile was not yet at parity with desktop.

- **Mobile was the headline feature.** The beta announcement said the v2 release introduces mobile support to Tauri, and the team called the release The Mobile Update.
- **Mobile scaffolding is in the stable release.** The stable announcement says the onboarding now also bootstraps mobile development templates for iOS and Android.
- **Native plugins are available.** The beta notes that there is support for notifications, dialogs, NFC, barcode reading, biometric authentication, clipboard and deep link.
- **Mobile was not fully mature at release.** The release candidate post said the team did not want to raise expectations that Tauri 2.0 will be the "mobile as a first class citizen" release, and it also acknowledged that not all of our desktop features and plugins are ported or available on mobile yet. It described feature parity and mobile development improvements as work for later minor releases.
- **Timing.** The release candidate post targeted the end of August for stable. The results don't include the exact stable release date, so check the official Tauri blog for that.

The official Tauri v2 docs cover the capabilities system, though most results were from the official site and third-party guides.

- **Where capabilities live:** Capability files are either defined as a JSON or a TOML file inside the src-tauri/capabilities directory. Capabilities can also be inlined in `tauri.conf.json`.
- **Enablement:** Per the official capabilities page, files in that directory are enabled automatically, but once capabilities are explicitly enabled in the tauri.conf.json, only these are used in the application build.
- **Default-deny model:** A third-party guide notes that unlike Tauri v1, where all IPC commands were accessible by default, Tauri v2 requires explicit permission grants.
- **Reference schema:** The capability reference page describes a description of what the capability is intended to allow on associated windows. Its fields include `permissions` (required), `platforms`, `remote`, `webviews`, and `windows`.
- **Core permissions:** The core permissions page lists every permission for the framework core, and if you are looking for permissions to specific Tauri plugins, please refer to the Plugins section of the documentation.
- **Common failure:** A community article says permission errors in the console typically look like a rejected Promise with a message such as plugin:shell|execute not allowed. It identifies the capabilities file as the first thing to check.
- **Multi-window and platform scoping:** The official docs show platform-specific files, such as one for desktop and one for mobile. A third-party guide notes that the capability's windows array must include the window label.
- **Best practice:** Community guides recommend least privilege, such as defining granular capabilities in src-tauri/capabilities/ instead of using wildcard permissions.

I did not open the pages themselves, so details may have changed. The official pages I'd check first are https://v2.tauri.app/security/capabilities/ and https://v2.tauri.app/reference/acl/capability/.

input.prompt: Does this page describe the capability-based permission system (capability files in src-tauri/capabilities, permissions granting access to commands, default-deny)? Quote the relevant sentences briefly.

toolu_01SDpKJvN9ttxECbGMHrpZP9.prompt: Does this page describe the capability-based permission system (capability files in src-tauri/capabilities, permissions granting access to commands, default-deny)? Quote the relevant sentences briefly.

content.content:
Yes, the page describes the capability-based system. It explains that capabilities control which permissions apply to which windows:

- "Capabilities define which permissions are granted or denied for which windows or webviews."
- "Capability files are either defined as a JSON or a TOML file inside the `src-tauri/capabilities` directory."

Each capability file lists permissions by identifier, such as `core:window:allow-set-title`, which grant access to specific APIs and commands.

The page does not use the term "default-deny." It describes a mixed default. Commands registered in the app are open by default: "are allowed to be used by all the windows and webviews of the app." Remote access is restricted by default: "By default the API is only accessible to bundled code shipped with the Tauri App." The page suggests `AppManifest::commands` to narrow command access.

content.text:
- Tauri 2.0 stable 릴리스(2024년 10월 2일 공개 페이지 기준)에 모바일 지원이 포함됐다. 블로그는 "A very much awaited part of this release is the mobile operating system support"라고 소개하며, 변경 로그에도 "Added Mobile support"가 있다 [1]
- 다만 모바일의 한계도 함께 명시돼 있다. "On mobile not all of the official plugins are supported"라고 적혀 있어, 모바일에서 모든 공식 플러그인이 지원되지는 않는다 [1]
- 권한은 capability 기반이다. "Capabilities define which permissions are granted or denied for which windows or webviews"이며, capability 파일은 `src-tauri/capabilities` 안의 JSON 또는 TOML로 정의된다 [2]. 단, 이 페이지는 "default-deny"라고 하지 않는다. 앱에 등록된 명령은 기본적으로 모든 창과 webview에서 쓸 수 있고, 원격 접근만 기본 제한된다 [2]

출처
1. [Tauri 2.0 Stable Release](https://v2.tauri.app/blog/tauri-20/)
2. [Security > Capabilities | Tauri](https://v2.tauri.app/security/capabilities/)
